text:
alex: quick help — I'm hunting a request from a user report. I only have a trace id: 7f4c3b2a. Console trace view shows spans but I can't see the x-request-id in the UI. Where's the fastest place to grab the raw request lines?
maria: start from the trace detail page and click 'Related logs' — that often links directly. if the console link is missing, CLI is fastest: try grepping proxy/edge logs by trace/span id. e.g.

maria: ```
stern -n prod 'proxy|edge' --since 1h | rg 7f4c3b2a
# or for a specific pod
kubectl logs -n prod edge-abc-123 -c envoy --since=10m | rg 7f4c3b2a
```
alex: stern is spitting a ton of output for me and pods rotate every few minutes, any tips to narrow it down?
sam: if pods rotate, first get the pod list and then check that range only:

sam: ```
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=edge -o name
kubectl logs -n prod <pod-name> -c envoy --since=5m | rg 7f4c3b2a
```
sam: also check the ingress/proxy namespace — sometimes the header is only logged there. we inject X-Trace-Id and X-Req-Id at the edge.
maria: if you have the exact timestamp: use stern --since 2m or --since-time to limit to the minute window. the trace->span detail sometimes includes service/host which points you to the right pod.
ops-bot: note: logs are retained hot for 7d; older logs require an archive restore request to infra-logs.
alex: nailed it — ran `stern -n prod edge --since 2m | rg 7f4c3b2a` and found the raw request line in edge-proxy. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
sam: one-liner if you want to save it: `stern -n prod edge -s --since 2m | rg 7f4c3b2a --line-number`
maria: :thumbsup: paste the full trace id if you want me to pull permalink from the console and cross-check.
